cited_theorems.statement_quote: Let Xn and Yn be martingales with EX2n < ∞ and EY2n < ∞. EXn Yn − EX0 Y0 = sum_{m=1}^n E(Xm − Xm−1)(Ym − Ym−1).

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{For the on-line case, set the parameters }S_1,S_2,\eta,\text{ and }q\text{ as in (3.4), and }K=\left\lfloor(4L\Delta n_0)\epsilon^{-2}\right\rfloor+1.\text{ Then under the Assumption 1, for Algorithm 1 with OPTION I, after }K\text{ iteration, we have }\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(\widetilde{x})\|]\le 5\epsilon.\text{ The gradient cost is bounded by }16L\Delta\sigma\cdot\epsilon^{-3}+2\sigma^2\epsilon^{-2}+4\sigma n_0^{-1}\epsilon^{-1}\text{ for any choice of }n_0\in[1,2\sigma/\epsilon].\text{ Treating }\Delta,L\text{ and }\sigma\text{ as positive constants, the stochastic gradient complexity is }O(\epsilon^{-3}).
main_theorem.rate: The online stochastic gradient complexity is O(epsilon^{-3}) when Delta, L, and sigma are treated as positive constants.

key_lemmas.role: This proves that the SPIDER gradient estimator maintains O(epsilon^2) mean-square error throughout an epoch.

reuse.reason: The inherited declaration is not directly instantiable: it requires Theorem1Schedule, theorem1RealizedScheduleAdmissible, and equalities S1=theorem1RefreshBatchCount, S2=theorem1RecursiveBatchCount, and q=theorem1EpochCount. The finite-sum route instead supplies the full-refresh boundary (B.17), S1=[n], S2=n^{1/2}/n_0, and q=n_0n^{1/2}; Theorem2_FiniteSum_Estimator_Error_Adapter is the named adapter that preserves the common SPIDER recurrence while replacing those online rounded-count and variance-bound prerequisites.

The inherited B.8 declaration is not schedule-agnostic at the Lean type level: it requires Theorem1Schedule P.L P.sigma epsilon n0 and derives n0>=1 through that online predicate. The finite-sum proof supplies only epsilon>0, L>0, 1<=n0, and the finite-sum Option II update; Theorem2_FiniteSum_OneStep_Descent_Adapter exposes the same B.8 inequality under exactly those finite-sum obligations and reuses the inherited pathwise algebra without importing the online sigma schedule.
The B.15 estimator-to-gradient conversion is main-theorem proof array index 11, where the finite-sum proof applies the inherited uniform-average bound without changing its mathematical content.
The finite-sum B.18 application is key-lemma proof array index 4 and uses the same Assumption 1(ii) averaged component-gradient Lipschitz bound with L_B=L, with no strengthening of smoothness.
